title: Development Stories Draft
description: Internal structured representation used while generating, enriching and validating development stories. Each story is saved twice under one Story ID: as an ultra-lean story in the '# Development Stories' Markdown section of the requirements document (Story ID, a concise summary label and one functional acceptance-criteria statement: 'summary' and 'lean_acceptance_criteria' below) and as a detailed story in the single consolidated file stories/detailed_stories.md (the 'detailed' object below, which also carries the non-functional requirements). The lean story is derived from the detailed story. Requirement and gap mappings are kept in stories/story-generation-state.json and are derived or recorded by scripts/sync-development-stories.py, never written into a story.

story_id.description: The existing ID for a story that is already in the document; null (or absent) for a genuinely new story. IDs for new stories are assigned by the sync script, never by the agent.

summary.description: A concise, meaningful one-line label of the story's core capability, typically 3-7 words (for example 'Registered user login'); understandable at a glance, not a full explanatory sentence. Shared by both representations: the heading of the story in the requirements document and in the detailed stories file.

lean_acceptance_criteria.description: The ULTRA-LEAN acceptance criteria written into the requirements document: exactly ONE concise statement covering all essential, confirmed functional outcomes and business rules, specific, observable and testable. Not several bullets, not Given/When/Then, no implementation detail, no non-functional criteria. Plain text without numbering or bullets.

detailed.description: The DETAILED story written into stories/detailed_stories.md, with every field below always rendered so all stories have the same structure.

description.description: The user need in the 'As a [user], I want [capability], so that [benefit].' form. Plain paragraphs separated by a blank line.

preconditions.description: What must be true before the story applies. Empty when the requirements state none.

functional_behaviour.description: The detailed functional behaviour the system must provide.

business_rules.description: The business rules, limits and constraints that apply, with the exact values. Empty when none are stated.

acceptance_criteria.description: Complete, independently testable Given/When/Then criteria covering every supported rule, validation, boundary and security condition. Plain text without numbering; numbering is added when the story is written.

scenarios.description: Relevant alternate and error scenarios. Empty when none are supported.

non_functional_requirements.description: Applicable non-functional requirements and quality attributes (performance, security, availability, accessibility, audit and so on) with their measurable targets. Empty when the requirements state none.

dependencies.description: Other stories, systems, data or decisions this story depends on. Empty when none are known.

lean_reviewed.description: True when this run derived the lean story from the detailed story, or confirmed that the existing lean story is still current. Clears the 'needs updating' flag the state keeps after a detailed story was edited.

source_requirement_ids.description: Atomic requirements this story is built from. Stored in the internal state only.

applied_decisions.description: IDs of resolved gaps whose latest recorded decision is reflected in this story. Stored in the internal state only.

not_covered_requirements.description: Atomic requirements that are deliberately not turned into a story, each with the reason.

decisions_reviewed.description: Resolved-gap decisions examined in this run. Only these advance the incorporation ledger. 'incorporated' needs a story listing the gap in applied_decisions; 'no_change_required' records an explicit determination that no story changes.
